related_questions.question: What are the new forbearance rules?

text_blocks.snippet: The most recent updates to mortgage forbearance rules stem from the CARES Act and subsequent extensions and regulations. Homeowners with federally-backed mortgages can request forbearance for up to 180 days, with the possibility of an additional 180-day extension upon request. Servicers must grant forbearance upon a borrower's attestation of COVID-related financial hardship, and no additional fees, penalties, or interest can be charged beyond the scheduled amounts. Upon expiration of the forbearance period, borrowers will need to work with their servicer to determine repayment options.
Key aspects of the current rules:

list.title: Eligibility:
list.snippet: Homeowners with federally-backed mortgages (FHA, VA, USDA, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac) experiencing a COVID-related financial hardship are eligible for forbearance.

list.title: Duration:
list.snippet: The initial forbearance period is up to 180 days, and borrowers can request an extension for another 180 days, for a total of up to 360 days.

list.title: No Fees or Penalties:
list.snippet: Servicers cannot charge additional interest, fees, or penalties for missed payments during the forbearance period.

list.title: Repayment:
list.snippet: Missed payments during forbearance must be repaid, but servicers are required to offer various repayment options, such as repayment plans, loan modifications, or other options, rather than requiring a lump-sum payment.

list.title: Servicer Obligations:
list.snippet: Servicers must inform borrowers about their repayment options and how to avoid foreclosure, including providing information about free housing counseling services.

list.title: No Foreclosure During Forbearance:
list.snippet: Servicers generally cannot start foreclosure proceedings during the forbearance period without first evaluating the borrower for available loss mitigation options.

list.title: Contact your servicer:
list.snippet: As soon as you anticipate difficulty making mortgage payments, contact your servicer to discuss your options and request forbearance if needed.

list.title: Understand your options:
list.snippet: Be sure to understand the repayment options available to you before entering forbearance, as they may vary depending on your loan type.

list.title: Keep records:
list.snippet: Keep detailed notes of all conversations with your servicer and review all documentation carefully.

list.title: Seek assistance:
list.snippet: If you are struggling to understand your options or disagree with your servicer, consider contacting a HUD-approved housing counselor for free, impartial advice.

related_questions.question: What is the forbearance rule?
related_questions.snippet: Forbearance is the intentional action of abstaining from doing something. In the context of the law, it refers to the act of delaying from enforcing a right, obligation, or debt. For example, a creditor may forbear legal action against the debtor if they settle the debt payment with new payment conditions.
